name: Lishmah (Offering for Its Own Sake)
notes: The requirement that offerings be sacrificed with proper intent for the specific type of offering; consequences of slaughtering not for its own sake (shelo lishmah)

name: Shinui Makom (Improper Location Intent for Offering)
notes: Disqualification of offerings due to intent to eat or burn sacrificial portions outside the designated area (chutz limkomo), distinct from pigul which involves intent beyond designated time

name: Four Sacrificial Rites (Arba Avodot)
notes: The four essential rites of sacrifice: slaughter, blood collection, conveying blood to altar, and sprinkling blood; disqualifying intent during any of these invalidates the offering

name: Kodshei Kodashim vs. Kodashim Kalim (Most Sacred vs. Lesser Sanctity)
notes: Distinction between offerings of the highest sanctity and offerings of lesser sanctity, with differences in location of slaughter, consumption, and who may eat them

name: Tzafon (Northern Section of Temple Courtyard)
notes: Requirement that offerings of the most sacred order be slaughtered in the northern section of the Temple courtyard; detailed laws of this location requirement

name: Number of Blood Placements (Matnot Dam)
notes: Rules governing required number of blood placements: one placement, two placements that are four, four placements on corners, and inner altar placements; consequences of omitting placements

name: Dam HaNefesh and Sheyarei HaDam (Soul Blood and Remainder Blood)
notes: Distinction between the initial blood spurting from the neck and the remainder blood; the remainder is poured at the base of the altar and its absence does not disqualify the offering

name: Yesod HaMizbeach (Base of the Altar)
notes: The base/foundation of the outer altar where remainder blood is poured; not all sides have a base, affecting where blood can be placed

name: Chut HaSikra (Red Line of the Altar)
notes: The red line running along the middle of the outer altar dividing it into upper and lower halves; blood of different offerings must be placed on the correct side of this line

name: Misuse Liability for Disqualified Offerings
notes: Whether disqualified offerings retain their consecrated status for purposes of misuse liability; relationship between sin offerings and burnt offerings that were changed in designation

name: Ascending the Altar – Shall Not Descend (Ya'aleh Lo Yeirid)
notes: Rule that disqualified offerings that have ascended the altar are not removed; distinction between items that may remain and items that must be removed; sanctification by the altar

name: Sanctification by the Altar (Kiddush Mizbeach)
notes: The principle that the altar sanctifies items suited to it; similarly the ramp and service vessels sanctify; items already on the altar are not removed even if disqualified

name: Tadir uMekudash (Precedence of Frequent and Sacred Offerings)
notes: Rules of priority in sacrificing offerings: more frequent offerings precede less frequent ones; more sacred offerings precede less sacred ones

name: Shechitat Chutz (Slaughtering Outside the Temple)
notes: Detailed laws of liability for slaughtering and offering sacrifices outside the Temple courtyard; conditions for liability including fitness of the animal and intent

name: History of Bamot (Private Altars — Permitted and Prohibited Periods)
notes: Historical progression of permitted and prohibited private altars: Tabernacle period, Gilgal, Shiloh, Nov, Gibeon, Jerusalem Temple; differences in laws of consumption at each location

name: Location of Eating Sacrificial Meat
notes: Rules governing where sacrificial meat may be eaten: within curtains (Temple courtyard), within Jerusalem walls, or anywhere; differences between most sacred and lesser sanctity offerings

name: Time Limit for Eating Sacrificial Meat (Zman Achilah)
notes: Time limits within which sacrificial meat must be consumed: one day and night (until midnight), two days and one night; consequences of eating after the permitted time (notar)

name: Notar (Leftover Sacrificial Meat)
notes: Prohibition against eating sacrificial meat left over beyond its permitted time; karet liability; distinction from pigul

name: Hides of Sacrificial Animals (Orot Kodashim)
notes: Rules governing who receives the hides of burnt offerings and other sacrificial animals; hides of burnt offerings go to priests; hides of offerings of lesser sanctity go to owners; conditions affecting this

name: Burning of Disqualified Offerings (Serifat Kodashim)
notes: Laws of burning disqualified offerings in the place of burning (beit hadeshen) or in the Temple courtyard; distinction between offerings burned outside Jerusalem and those burned inside

name: Garment Impurity from Burning Communal Sin Offerings
notes: Kohanim who burn the bulls and goats that are burned outside Jerusalem render their garments impure; when this occurs and when it does not

name: Blood of Sin Offering on Garments
notes: Laws requiring laundering of garments on which sin offering blood was sprayed; applies to both eaten and burned sin offerings; must be laundered in the sacred area

name: Cooking Vessels for Sacrificial Meat — Scouring and Rinsing
notes: Requirement to scour and rinse copper vessels in which sin offerings were cooked; must be done in the sacred area; distinction between earthenware (broken) and copper (scoured and rinsed) vessels

name: Mixtures of Different Bloods
notes: Laws governing when blood of different offerings become mixed; rules for presenting mixed bloods on altar; blood of fit offerings mixed with unfit bloods; blood requiring inner vs. outer presentation

name: Mixtures of Sacrificial Limbs and Animals
notes: Laws when sacrificial animals or their limbs become intermixed; solutions including letting them graze until blemished, selling, eating by most stringent rule

name: Bird Sin Offering Rites (Melikah and Dam)
notes: Detailed rites of the bird sin offering: melikah at nape, sprinkling blood below red line, squeezing blood at base; differences from bird burnt offering

name: Bird Burnt Offering Rites
notes: Detailed rites of the bird burnt offering: melikah at nape with separation of head, squeezing blood at upper altar, removal of crop and feathers, rending the body

name: Impurity of Bird Carcasses (Neveilat Of)
notes: Unique impurity of bird carcasses transmitted through swallowing (beit habeli'ah); how melikah prevents this impurity even for tereifa birds; debate between Rabbi Meir, Rabbi Yehuda, Rabbi Yosi

name: Distribution of Sacrificial Meat Among Priests
notes: Rules for which priests receive a share of sacrificial meat; priests unfit for service on a given day do not receive a share; relationship between sprinkling blood and receiving a share

name: Offerings of Gentiles (Korban Goyim)
notes: Special rules for offerings consecrated by gentiles: not subject to piggul, notar, or eating-in-impurity prohibitions; liability for slaughtering outside the Temple

name: Six Intentions Required for Sacrificial Rites
notes: The six matters for which an offering must be slaughtered: for the sake of its type, its owner, God, consumption by fire, aroma, pleasing God; plus atonement for sin offerings and guilt offerings

name: Laws Unique to the Tabernacle vs. Private Altars
notes: Specific rites that apply only at the Tabernacle/Temple and not at private altars: semichah, slaughter in north, blood placements, waving, bringing to corner; piggul, notar, and impurity apply equally

name: Service Performed by Disqualified Priest
notes: Effect of Temple service performed by various disqualified priests (impure, lacking vestments, tevul yom, mechusar kapparah, onen, uncircumcised) on the validity of the offering
